 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Clemson Tigers have seen better days, both this current college football season and as a program overall.
 There has been a lot of frustration around the program of late, with the Tigers underperforming once again. Calls for head coach Dabo Swinney to be fired have started to come in again.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Clemson currently holds a record of 6-4 on the season, with the team coming off a tough loss to the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets last week.
 The Tigers scored just six points last week against Georgia Tech, with injuries taking over the offense again. But the Clemson offense has been a problem all year, and it just continued against the Yellow Jackets, despite the game being at home.
 This week, Clemson will be heading out on the road to take on the Duke Blue Devils, giving them another test to overcome. Duke has played very well this season, with them holding a record of 7-3 for the year.
 The Blue Devils are coming off a close loss to the Miami Hurricanes last week, and they will likely be looking to end the year on a high note. Clemson will have to overcome a Duke team determined for redemption this week, mixed with a road night game, which are never easy in college football.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Heading into the game, the Tigers are heavy underdogs, with the Blue Devils being viewed much more highly. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Clemson only has a 20.9 percent chance of winning the game against Duke.
 Mixing in how poorly the Tigers have played of late, with the problems on offense, it could be tough to overcome this Blue Devils team. Clemson is going to have to find a way to generate points, especially against a tough Duke offense.
 The Tigers will be starting fifth-year quarterback Trent Pearman under center in the game, following an injury to Tait Reynolds last week. Pearman has appeared in three games for Clemson this week, throwing for 86 yards and two interceptions.
 Against Duke, Pearman will have to figure out a way to get the offense going, giving this team a spark to work with. Clemson has struggled to move the ball on opponents all season long, and Duke has seen a feisty defense take place.
 Kickoff for the game between the Tigers and the Blue Devils is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET from Durham.
